clue.text: They report pot, aluminium, is found between beams

indicators.note: the pot and the metal sit between the beams, so they go inside that word

parts.note: joists are the beams that hold up a floor
an urn is a large pot or vase
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A builder finds a pot of aluminium wedged between the floor beams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' reads as a cooking vessel or cannabis but here is a vase-like urn.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists are the people whose job is to report the news, so 'They report' describes them.

clue.text: Crow picked up roll beneath sailor

indicators.note: in a down answer, the second piece sits below the sailor

parts.note: Jack (as in Jack Tar) is a traditional name for a sailor

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the word up means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: a wad is a roll of banknotes

explanation.surface: A sailor has a bread roll that a crow swoops down and steals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' reverses WAD to DAW, placed under JACK.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackdaw is a small grey-naped bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Not coloured at all edges — uneven dainty emerald

indicators.note: only the outside letters of each of the three following words are taken

explanation.surface: A craftsman complains that an uneven dainty emerald has lost its colour around the rim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at all edges' takes the first and last letters of uneven, dainty and emerald: UN, DY, ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something undyed has had no dye applied, so it is left in its natural, uncoloured state.

clue.text: Scandinavians assembled gear in snow

indicators.note: putting the letters together into a new structure signals rearranging them

explanation.surface: A group of northerners get their kit together out in the snow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembled' rearranges GEAR IN SNOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is a Scandinavian country, so its people are Scandinavians.

clue.text: Branch from ascent leaving summit

indicators.note: in a down answer the summit is the top letter, which is dropped

parts.note: a climb is an ascent

explanation.surface: A climber falls from a branch while descending from the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving summit' takes the C off the top of CLIMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb of a tree is one of its large branches.

clue.text: Fancy room aboard ship for weapons

indicators.note: being aboard means being inside the ship, so these pieces sit within it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a fancy is a notion or idea

explanation.surface: An elegant cabin on board a vessel is used to store arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective describing the room, but it is a noun meaning a notion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidearms are pistols or swords carried at the side, a class of personal weapon.

clue.text: Unique player really is welcomed by crowd

parts.note: so can mean really, as in 'so good'

indicators.note: being welcomed by a crowd means being taken into it, so the word goes inside

parts.note: a lot is a group or crowd of people

explanation.surface: A one-of-a-kind performer is genuinely embraced by the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unique player' together is the definition: a soloist is the one player performing.
explanation.definitionFit: A soloist plays alone, the single performer of a piece, hence a unique player.

clue.text: Equestrian bathed in Olympic adoration

indicators.note: the answer is immersed inside the run of these words

explanation.surface: A rider at the Games is basking in the crowd's adoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bathed in' points to the letters inside olymPIC ADORation.
explanation.definitionFit: A picador is the mounted man in a bullfight who goads the bull with a lance, so a horseman.

clue.text: Heavy machines Greek character guided over waterways

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first pieces sit over the last

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
led means guided
rivers are natural waterways

explanation.surface: A Greek steered heavy equipment across the canals.
explanation.definitionFit: Pile-drivers are large machines that hammer posts into the ground.

clue.text: Before circuit, regularly cleared mould off bike part

indicators.note: the letters picked come before the lap
every other letter is taken away, leaving alternate letters

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track

explanation.surface: Before a race lap, a rider wiped mould off part of the bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly cleared' keeps the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of the two words, and 'Before' places them ahead of the circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mudflap hangs behind a wheel of a bicycle or vehicle to stop dirt spraying up.

clue.text: Metacarpal remedied with injection of ordinary drug

indicators.note: the letter is injected into the rearranged letters
a thing remedied has been fixed or reworked, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken hand bone was treated with an injection of a common painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remedied' rearranges METACARPAL, and 'with injection of' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Paracetamol is a widely used painkilling medicine, a common drug.

clue.text: Son of Parisian visibly embarrassed having runs

parts.note: a lad is a boy or son
de is French for of
someone visibly embarrassed has gone red

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's son blushes because he has a stomach upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Laddered tights or stockings have runs, lines of unravelled stitches.

clue.text: Without leader, window-fitter becomes less diligent

indicators.note: the first letter, the one that leads the word, is dropped

parts.note: a glazier fits glass into windows

explanation.surface: Lacking a foreman, a glass-fitter starts slacking off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without leader' removes G from GLAZIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazier is the comparative of lazy, describing someone who puts in less effort.

clue.text: We're told, escape little figure that's shabby

indicators.note: points to what something sounds like when spoken rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: to flee is to escape
a bit is a little
ten is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: Someone reports fleeing a small, scruffy sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We're told' turns FLEE into the same-sounding FLEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Flea-bitten means worn and scruffy, as if infested by fleas.

clue.text: Professor coming round with drink

indicators.note: the professor goes round the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: An academic recovers consciousness holding a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming round' wraps DON round W.
explanation.definitionFit: To down a drink is to swallow it in one go.

clue.text: Tactful cop with mass in Capitol running riot

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector

indicators.note: letters that run riot are thrown into disorder, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A sensitive policeman deals with crowds in the Capitol during a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running riot' rearranges M with CAPITOL to give PLOMATIC; 'in' just says the mass joins the building's letters. 'Capitol' is the US Congress building.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplomatic means handling people with tact and sensitivity, like a diplomat.

clue.text: Sea raid, act deployed to gain island

indicators.note: the rearranged letters gain a letter inside them
troops deployed are arranged into new positions, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A naval raid is launched to capture an island at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges the eight letters of the two words into ADRATIC, and 'to gain' takes the island letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adriatic is the arm of the Mediterranean between Italy and the Balkans.

clue.text: Accompanying cool revolutionary in charge of chopper

parts.note: in means fashionable or cool

indicators.note: something revolving turns round, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: dental means relating to teeth, and choppers is slang for teeth

explanation.surface: A calm rebel takes charge of a helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses IC to CI. 'Chopper' looks like a helicopter or axe but is slang for a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Incidental means occurring alongside something more important, so accompanying it.

clue.text: Groups providing tips about upcoming panel show

indicators.note: the hints go around the reversed show

parts.note: clues are tips or hints

indicators.note: in a down answer coming up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: QI is a British television comedy quiz panel show

explanation.surface: Teams supply hints about a panel show that is coming soon.
explanation.walkthrough: QI is a long-running British TV comedy quiz panel show; 'upcoming' turns it upside down in this down entry, and 'about' wraps the tips round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cliques are small exclusive groups of people.

clue.text: Hollow animal home, sett abandoned by group

parts.note: a den is a wild animal's home

indicators.note: the group leaves the word, so its letters are removed

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: A badger's burrow lies empty, deserted by its family.
explanation.walkthrough: A sett is a badger's burrow. 'abandoned by' removes SET from SETT, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: A dent is a small hollow pressed into a surface.

clue.text: Raising hat, is head of theatre snobbish?

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means reading upward, so backwards

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Is the theatre director a snob for doffing his hat?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising' reverses TILE to ELIT. 'head of' gives T from theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: An elitist believes in rule by a select few, so looks down on others, like a snob.

clue.text: Charge fine car up keeping close to motor

indicators.note: the reversed letters hold the next letter inside them
in a down answer, going up means the letters read backwards

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
a Fiat is a make of car

indicators.note: the close of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A fine for a car parked up includes a charge near the motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses F FIAT to TAIFF, and 'keeping' holds R, the 'close to motor', inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a fee or a list of charges, for example a duty on imports.

clue.text: Obtain licence finally authorised

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: licit means lawful or authorised

explanation.surface: At last a permit is granted officially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E from licence.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out or obtain a response or information.

clue.text: Metal bird overturned in a dump uncovered

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: turning the two words over reads them backwards
taking off the covers removes the outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: A bird is found upside down at the rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses IN A to ANI. 'uncovered' strips the ends of dump, leaving UM.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanium is a strong, light, silvery chemical element classed as a metal.

clue.text: Beat back in frenzied massage

indicators.note: the back of the word is its last letter, which is taken

parts.note: to rub is to massage

explanation.surface: A masseur pounds a client's back in a wild session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back in' takes D, the last letter of frenzied.
explanation.definitionFit: To drub is to beat thoroughly, either physically or in a contest.

clue.text: Quiet voice that provides cover

parts.note: sh is the sound used to call for quiet
to voice something is to utter it

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken voice offers protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A shutter is a hinged panel that covers a window.

clue.text: Minor test involving hospital equipment

indicators.note: the test takes the equipment in, holding it inside

parts.note: a trial is a test
an IV is an intravenous drip used in hospitals

explanation.surface: A small medical trial uses some hospital kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The hospital equipment is an intravenous drip, abbreviated to its two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial means of little importance, which is what minor means.

clue.text: Money for ill people if neck bites degenerated

indicators.note: letters that have degenerated have fallen into disorder, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Insect bites on the neck worsening may qualify someone for welfare payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'degenerated' rearranges IF NECK BITES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sick benefit is a state payment to people too unwell to work.
